newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH NUCLEAR PLANT TENDER ATTRACTS FOUR FIRMS.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH NUCLEAR PLANT TENDER ATTRACTS FOUR FIRMS.

text.p: Four foreign companies requested information on Turkey's tender for construction of the country's first nuclear power station, an official from the state power utility company TEAS said.
"There are four firms who purchased the bidding specifications," the official told Reuters.
He said the firms were: Canada's AECL, French-German venture NPI, Westinghouse -Mitsubishi Elec. and Italy's Ansaldo.
The four companies had already sought information by the original deadline of January 20, when the expiry date was extended at the request of other companies to the end of January.
No more companies have since requested the bidding details, the TEAS official said.
The plant is to be built near the village of Akkuyu on the Mediterranean as part of Turkey's plans to increase energy production in the face of sharp rises in demand.
An initial bid clarification meeting for the Akkuyu plant is expected to be held in the second week of March, followed by a second meeting late in May, the official said.

TEAS is to collect by June 30 bids for the plant, which is to be fully financed by the builder on a turn-key basis. The project will cost $2 billion to $4 billion depending on the choice of two options.

The first is a plant of one or more units with a capacity ranging from 800 MegaWatts (MW) to 1,400 MW. The other option's range is between 2,400 to 2,800 MW. Each power production unit in both options should have a capacity of 600 MW or more.
